{{Current events|year=2026|month=05|day=7|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations]]
****[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]]
*****[[Pakistan]] [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Pakistan)|foreign office]] spokesperson Tahir Andrabi says that a [[ceasefire]] agreement between [[Iran]] and the [[United States]] to end the war is expected "sooner rather than later". [https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2642661/pakistan (''Arab News PK'')]
*****[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] says that the [[ceasefire]] is still in effect despite the recent strikes on the [[List of destroyers of the United States Navy|U.S. destroyers]]. [https://abcnews.com/Politics/trump-calls-iran-strikes-love-tap-ceasefire-effect/story?id=132762926 (ABC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-sees-swift-end-war-iran-reviews-us-peace-proposal-2026-05-07/ (Reuters)]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****The Iranian Ports and Maritime Organization says that [[List of ports in Iran|ports in Iran]] are prepared to provide maritime services, technical support, supplies, and medical assistance to ships operating in the [[Strait of Hormuz]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-says-ports-ready-to-provide-support-services-to-ships-in-strait-of-hormuz/3929651 (AA)] [https://m.economictimes.com/news/international/world-news/iran-expresses-full-readiness-to-provide-maritime-services-technical-support-to-commercial-ships-in-hormuz/articleshow/130875200.cms (''The Economic Times'')]
****A U.S. official tells ''[[Axios (website)|Axios]]'' that Iran and the U.S. have reportedly exchanged fire at the [[Strait of Hormuz]], with Iran claiming to strike three [[United States Navy|U.S. Navy]] ships and the U.S. claiming to strike targets on the waterway. [https://www.axios.com/2026/05/07/us-iran-hormuz-strait-fire-exchange (''Axios'')] [https://apnews.com/article/iran-us-israel-war-may-7-2026-fdc6d2ae9396377919c967746fa9996b (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-sees-swift-end-war-iran-reviews-us-peace-proposal-2026-05-07/ (Reuters)]
****The [[United States Central Command|U.S. Central Command]] confirms that [[United States Armed Forces|the military]] carried out "self-defense" [[May 2026 United States strikes on Iran|strikes]] against [[Islamic Republic of Iran Armed Forces|military]] facilities in response to Iran's attacks on the [[Arleigh Burke-class destroyer|Arleigh Burke]]-class destroyers [[USS Truxtun (DDG-103)|USS ''Truxtun'']], [[USS Rafael Peralta|USS ''Rafael Peralta'']], and [[USS Mason (DDG-87)|USS ''Mason'']] as the three ships were transiting the Hormuz into the [[Gulf of Oman]]. [https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026050806582342544 (''The Asia Business Daily'')] [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/05/07/politics/us-forces-strike-military-facilities-in-iran (CNN)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/us-confirms-striking-iran-in-self-defense-says-it-does-not-seek-escalation/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***Several explosions are heard at a port in [[Qeshm, Hormozgan|Qeshm]] and [[Bandar Abbas]] in Iran's [[Hormozgan province]]. [[Israel]] denies any involvement in the explosion, while [[Fox News]] reporter [[Jennifer Griffin]] says that the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] was behind the explosions. Officials say that the explosions does not mean the restart of the war or the end of the ceasefire. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/us-israel-iran-war/israel-denies-involvement-in-explosions-in-southern-iran/3930708 (AA)] [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260507-live-explosions-heard-in-several-iranian-cities-including-in-naval-port-of-bandar-abbas (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-military-strikes-irans-qeshm-port-bandar-abbas-fox-news-reporter-says-2026-05-07/ (Reuters)]
**[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
***[[Gaza war]]
****Azzam Al-Hayya, the son of [[List of leaders of Hamas|Hamas Political Bureau]] [[Chairman of the Hamas Political Bureau|chairman]] [[Khalil al-Hayya]], is confirmed by a [[Hamas]] official to have been killed during a [[Israel]] airstrike last night. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-attack-kills-son-hamas-leader-negotiating-with-trump-led-board-2026-05-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]], [[Kivu conflict]], [[Ituri conflict]]
**Forty people are killed and homes are [[Arson|burned]] by [[Allied Democratic Forces]] militants during attacks in [[North Kivu]] and [[Ituri Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-attacks-villages-allied-democratic-forces-killings-563bef10f07e476759c2738b820a6091 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2026 Cuban crisis]]
**[[Sherritt International]] suspends its mining operations in [[Cuba]] and withdraws expatriate staff, citing the risk of expanded [[United States embargo against Cuba|United States sanctions]] affecting its operations. [https://www.newsabhiyan.com/news-details.php?nid=407557 (AFP via News Abhiyan)]
*[[Tariffs in the second Trump administration]]
**The [[United States Court of International Trade|U.S. Court of International Trade]] rules that the 10% global tariffs imposed by [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]] are illegal. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/07/business/economy/trump-global-tariff-ruled-illegal.html (''The New York Times'')] 
*[[Mastercard]] says that they are planning to resume services in [[Syria]] for the first time in [[Syrian revolution|15 years]]. [https://sana.sy/en/economic/2315165/ (SANA)] [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/mastercard-prepares-to-launch-services-in-syria-after-15-years/3930746 (AA)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 15 people are killed and dozens of others are trapped when a gold mine [[Mining accident|collapses]] in [[West Pokot County]], [[Kenya]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/10-women-among-15-killed-as-gold-mine-collapses-in-northwestern-kenya/3931545 (AA)]
*Ten people are killed in a road accident involving a truck carrying a 40-foot container near [[Freetown]], [[Sierra Leone]]. [https://english.news.cn/africa/20260508/d5f81ef77a4f46658b48b5f99c719b44/c.html (Xinhua)]
*At least five people are killed and more than 12 others are injured in a large fire at a [[shopping mall]] in [[Los Mochis]], [[Sinaloa]], [[Mexico]]. [https://bnonews.com/index.php/2026/05/mall-fire-in-northwestern-mexico-leaves-people-injured-others-trapped/ (BNO News)]
*At least five people are killed in a fire at a [[fair]] in [[Villahermosa]], [[Tabasco]], Mexico. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/raging-fire-mexican-fairground-kills-five-authorities-say-2026-05-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*Two children are reported to have died from [[tuberculosis]] at displacement camps in [[Tawila]], [[North Darfur]], [[Sudan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/313635 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Cambodia–Thailand relations]]
**[[2025 Cambodian–Thai border crisis]]
***[[Cambodia]] and [[Thailand]] agree to restore relations following talks mediated by the [[Philippines]] on the sidelines of the 48th [[ASEAN Summit]] in [[Cebu]]. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/3251378/leaders-vow-to-rebuild-relations (''Bangkok Post'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/thai-cambodian-leaders-meet-asean-sidelines-amid-uneasy-truce-2026-05-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 South Korean martial law crisis]]
**The [[Seoul High Court]] reduces former [[South Korea]]n [[Prime Minister of South Korea|prime minister]] [[Han Duck-soo]]'s prison sentence from 23 years to 15 years for crimes related to former [[President of South Korea|president]] [[Yoon Suk Yeol]]'s 2024 [[martial law]] declaration, citing a lack of evidence that Han played a leading or [[premeditated]] role in the declaration. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/east-asia/south-korea-han-duck-soo-sentence-appeal-martial-law-6105741 (AFP via CNA)]
*[[Anti-corruption campaign under Xi Jinping]]
**Former [[China|Chinese]] [[Minister of National Defense (China)|defense ministers]] [[Li Shangfu]] and [[Wei Fenghe]] are both [[Capital punishment in China|sentenced to death]] with a two-year [[Death sentence with reprieve|reprieve]] following their convictions on [[Graft (politics)|graft]] charges. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clypjx383j2o (BBC News)] [https://www.politico.eu/article/china-sentences-two-former-ministers-to-suspended-death-penalty/ (''Politico'')]
*[[2026 Canvas security incident]]
**The [[ShinyHunters]] [[cybercrime]] group claims responsibility for breaching [[Instructure Holdings|Instructure Canvas]], a web-based [[learning management system]], a second time, affecting at least 275 million teachers and students worldwide. [https://www.trtworld.com/article/a4245b00f866 (TRT World)]
*[[Trafficking of Chinese nationals to scam centers abroad]]
**[[Sri Lanka]]n [[Sri Lanka Police|authorities]] arrest 30 [[China|Chinese]] and [[Vietnam]]ese nationals in [[Colombo]] in a crackdown on [[cybercrime|cyberscams]] in the country, raising the total number of those detained to 261. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/south-asia/sri-lanka-arrests-more-than-260-foreigners-over-cyberscams (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 United Kingdom local elections]]
**[[2026 Scottish Parliament election]], [[2026 Senedd election]]
***Voters in [[England]] elect six [[Directly elected mayors in England|mayors]] and 5,066 council seats across 136 [[List of county councils in England|councils]]. In [[Scotland]], voters elect 129 seats to the [[Scottish Parliament]]. In [[Wales]], voters elect 96 seats to the [[Senedd]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/c1428pev1n0t (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/ng-interactive/2026/may/07/local-elections-2026-may-full-results-england-scotland-wales (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Politics of Solomon Islands]]
**The [[National Parliament of Solomon Islands|parliament]] of the [[Solomon Islands]] debates a [[no-confidence motion]] against [[Prime Minister of Solomon Islands|prime minister]] [[Jeremiah Manele]]. The debate is a culmination of a [[political crisis]] that started with mass resignations of the cabinet on 16 March, recently escalated by a ruling on 1 May by the [[Judiciary of Solomon Islands|Court of Appeal]] ordering the reconvening of Parliament. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/pacific/594356/manele-calls-parliament-for-thursday-to-face-no-confidence-motion (RNZ)]
**Manele is ousted from the premiership following a successful no-confidence motion of 26–22, with two [[member of parliament|MPs]] absent. Manele remains as [[Caretaker government|caretaker]] prime minister until [[Governor-General of Solomon Islands|governor-general]] [[David Tiva Kapu]] declares a new prime minister. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/solomon-islands-pm-ousted-after-losing-confidence-vote-2026-05-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[2027 Salvadoran legislative election]], [[Right of Salvadoran expatriates to vote]]
**The [[Legislative Assembly of El Salvador|Legislative Assembly]] of [[El Salvador]] approves a [[Constitution of El Salvador|constitutional]] [[Constitutional amendment|reform]] that establishes an [[overseas constituency]] for [[Salvadorans|Salvadoran]] expatriates. The constituency is allocated 6 seats in the 60-seat legislature. [https://www.laprensagrafica.com/elsalvador/cuantos-diputados-tendra-la-diaspora-salvadorena-20260507-0068.html (''La Prensa Gráfica'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]

'''Sports'''
*[[International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Belarus at the Olympics]]
***The [[International Olympic Committee]] lifts restrictions on [[Belarus]]ian [[Belarus at the Olympics|athletes]] participating in the [[Olympic Games]] from [[2028 Summer Olympics|2028]], while [[Russia]]n [[Russia at the Olympics|athletes]] remain limited to [[Authorised Neutral Athletes|individual neutral participation]] because of the [[Russian Olympic Committee]]'s suspension. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/olympic-games/20260507-ioc-lifts-olympic-ban-on-belarus-but-russia-still-suspended (AFP via RFI)] [https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/articles/cy82720dnydo (BBC News)]
*[[2027 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], [[2027 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament]]
**In [[basketball]], the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|men's]] and [[NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament|women's]] tournaments will expand to 76 teams beginning next year. [https://apnews.com/article/march-madness-ncaa-expansion-5430c958e232afd8eb9226aa255e9c76 (AP)] [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7261356/2026/05/07/ncaa-tournament-expansion-76-teams-2027/ (''The Athletic via The New York Times'')]
